cards: Cyrus the Great, or Cyrus II, was the founder of the Achaemenid Empire, who acceded in 559 BCE as king of Anshan.
Darius I, also known as Darius the Great, was king of the Achaemenid Empire (r. 522–486 BCE).
Confucius (Kong Qiu, Kongzi) was a teacher and minor official of the State of Lu whose sayings, collected by his disciples in the Analects, became the basis of Confucianism.
Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, Tarquin the Proud, was by tradition the seventh and last king of Rome.
Croesus was the last king of Lydia in western Anatolia, ruling in the sixth century BCE and proverbial for his wealth.
Alyattes was king of Lydia from around 610 to 560 BCE, of the Mermnad dynasty, and father of Croesus.
r. c. 610–560 BCE · Ancient Near East
Solon was an Athenian statesman, lawgiver and poet.
Jeremiah was a Hebrew prophet in Jerusalem from the late 7th century BCE until after its destruction by the Babylonians in 587 BCE.
Thales of Miletus was a Greek thinker of the 6th century BCE, traditionally regarded as the first philosopher and the first of the Seven Sages.
Astyages was the last king of the Median Empire in the sixth century BCE.
Gelon was tyrant of Gela from about 491 BCE and of Syracuse from 485 BCE.
Harpagus was a Median noble who, according to Herodotus, saved the infant Cyrus from death ordered by King Astyages and later helped Cyrus overthrow him around 550 BCE.
Peisistratus was a tyrant of Athens who seized power three times between about 561 and 546 BCE and ruled until his death in 527 BCE.
Polycrates was tyrant of Samos from about 538 to 522 BCE.
Lars Porsenna was an Etruscan king of Clusium (modern Chiusi) who, in Roman tradition, attacked Rome around 508 BCE after the expulsion of its last king, Tarquinius Superbus.
Lucretia was, according to Roman tradition, a noblewoman whose rape by Sextus Tarquinius, son of the king, and her subsequent suicide provoked the overthrow of the Roman monarchy in 509 BCE.
Pythagoras was a Greek philosopher from Samos who, by tradition to escape the tyranny of Polycrates, settled at Croton in southern Italy around 530 BCE.
Sun Tzu (Sunzi, Sun Wu) is the traditional author of The Art of War, the most famous Chinese work on military strategy.
fl. c. 500 BCE · Central & East Asia
Aesop was a Greek storyteller to whom a large collection of fables, the Aesopica, is attributed.
Jehoiachin was a king of Judah who surrendered Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar II in 597 BCE.
Megabazus was a Persian general of Darius I in the late 6th century BCE.
Oroetes was the Persian satrap of Sardis under Cyrus the Great and Cambyses II.
Pactyes was a Lydian whom Cyrus the Great put in charge of the treasury of Lydia after its conquest around 546 BCE.
Sappho was a Greek lyric poet of Lesbos, active in Mytilene around 600 BCE.
Servius Tullius was, according to Roman tradition, the sixth king of Rome, reigning in the 6th century BCE.
Alcaeus was a Greek lyric poet of Mytilene on Lesbos and a contemporary of Sappho.
Anacreon was a Greek lyric poet from Teos in Ionia, famous for short songs about love and wine.
Anaximander of Miletus was a Greek philosopher of the 6th century BCE and a pupil of Thales in the Milesian school.
Democedes of Croton was a Greek physician of the 6th century BCE.
Histiaeus was the tyrant of Miletus under the Persian king Darius I in the late 6th century BCE.
Miltiades was an Athenian general who ruled the Thracian Chersonese before fleeing to Athens from the Persians in 493 BCE.
Phalaris was tyrant of Acragas in Sicily from about 570 to 554 BCE.
Pittacus was a statesman of Mytilene on Lesbos, counted among the Seven Sages of Greece.
Skunkha was a chief of the Saka Tigraxauda, the 'pointed-cap' Saka of Central Asia, in the late 6th century BCE.
fl. c. 520 BCE · Central & East Asia
Xenophanes of Colophon was a Greek poet and philosopher who left Ionia after the Persian conquest and spent a long life wandering the Greek world, especially Sicily.
Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon in 597 BCE.
Belshazzar was the son of Nabonidus, the last king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and governed Babylon as regent for about a decade while his father lived at the Arabian oasis of Tayma.
d. c. 539 BCE · Ancient Near East
Chersiphron of Knossos was a Cretan architect of the sixth century BCE who, with his son Metagenes, designed and began the archaic Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the first great marble temples…
Eupalinos of Megara was a Greek engineer of the sixth century BCE who built the aqueduct tunnel on Samos for the tyrant Polycrates.
Hipponax of Ephesus was a Greek iambic poet of the sixth century BCE who was expelled from Ephesus by its tyrants and lived at Clazomenae.
